title: PLUR1BUS Engine Contract
description: Pinned engine contract 1.17.0 with additive A1 curated-memory members. Runtime ports and cancellation remain hand-written Rust contracts.

ContractVersion.title: ContractVersion
ContractVersion.description: types/engine.d.ts — the frozen PLUR1BUS engine contract. Contract version 1.17.0 (frozen at 1.0.0 on 2026-09-22, owner decision B8; amended seventeen times under the policy below — see the changelog at the end of this header). This file reconciles the four places Phase 0 sketched the same API differently (review-report finding S4). Where ADR-002 and engine-extraction.md §b.2 disagreed, B8 chose: - `Principal.trust: "proved" | "inferred"`   (not `proof: "transport"`) - `TurnOrigin` as a string union plus a separate `AgentContext` (not one `TurnOrigin` object) - `capture()` returns a non-blocking `CaptureHandle` (not `Promise<CaptureResult>`) - `RecallResult.degraded` is a structured object or null (not a boolean) `createEngine` (engine/create-engine.js) implements it from M1b-1 on. It is the shape both the plugin host adapter and the harness are written against, and it is checked by `npm run typecheck`. Amendment policy: "frozen" means 1.0.0 is never edited in place. Any change to an exported member's shape that an existing adapter could observe — a new required property, a removed or renamed member, a narrowed or widened union, a changed parameter or return type — forces a `ContractVersion` bump; only additions no adapter can observe (a comment, a new optional property on a type the engine alone constructs) may land without one. `ContractVersion`, the assertions in `types/engine.conformance.ts` and both adapters move together in a single PR, so the contract, its gate and its two consumers are never in disagreement at any commit. Changelog: 1.1.0 — SecurePathResult.reason gains "acl-tool-unavailable" (Task 5). 1.2.0 — HostServices.workspaceDir becomes async (Task 6). 1.3.0 — HostServices.configPath(), HostServices.routing?, HostServices.pathOverrides? (G1 closure, M1b-1 Task 11). 1.4.0 — Engine surface of createEngine (M1b-1): ContextBlock.chars; RecallResult.timing (replaces timings) and .deferrals; RecallQuery.budget optional; JobRun/JobRegistry/JobSpec per spec 3.3 (outcome gains "abandoned"); CheckpointReason gains "session-end"; Engine.close({ budgetMs }); Engine.channels; HostServices.capabilities?; EngineEventName gains recall.block-clipped/-dropped, recall.completed; createEngine testOptions. 1.4.1 — JobTrigger gains "unknown" (a crash row recovered from a corrupt, unreadable start marker; M1b-1 final review m2). 1.5.0 — MemoryOps types, Engine.memory (E1 Task 2); runCommand deprecated; MemoryState.tombstones number | null (E1-R11); HostCapabilities.memoryArchiveDir? (E1 Task 8). 1.6.0 — AdminOps.share/forget alias Engine.memory (deprecated); ObsidianOps with explicit paths; migrate over a store schema marker; MemoryOps.propose/proposals (D31); MemoryCard.sharedBy/sourceId; MemoryOpError.detail; "memory.proposal" event; EngineStatus.storeSchema (E2). 1.7.0 — EmbeddingService.probe(opts?) → EmbeddingProbeResult (identity, readiness, memoized); serve(address?: IpcAddress | null) → EmbeddingServeResult (real scoped IPC, in-process owner, no claim listener); HostCapabilities.pushCriticalButtons? typed (E3). 1.8.0 — EngineStatus.jobs/models/journal/sharedMemory, degraded derived from model readiness; Engine.models (status, warm); HostCapabilities.journalBacklog?; MemoryOpErrorCode "unsupported"; CaptureResult.reason "duplicate-turn" (E4). 1.9.0 — engine-config.schema.json with readAt/x-tier/x-sensitive and its types (EngineConfigSchema, EngineConfigKey, EngineConfigReadAt); RecallQuery.warmOnly; RecallTiming.totalMs covers queue wait and prelude (E5). 1.10.0 — additive engine-config keys from the 7.18.5–7.18.20 port (runtime.deferPostTurnLlm, diaryFromUserChats, captureChunkingJev, recall.fullTextTopRecords/fullTextMaxChars) and JobName "post-turn-refine"; adapter-only keys stay on the plugin host manifest; no breaking change to existing callers. 1.11.0 — MemoryOps.import (finished-card ingest with deterministic ids) and Engine.stores.adopt (copy-never-move store take-over with a sample cosine probe for legacy stores); MemoryCard.provenance/sourceRef optional; no breaking change to existing callers. 1.12.0 — MemoryOps.rebind / MemoryOps.unbind (manual N:1 channel-identity link; user-scope owner metadata only) and ADOPT_PROBE_MIN_ROWS = min(8, available); UserPrincipal accepts user:v1 and user:v2; MemoryOpErrorCode "identity-already-bound" | "ledger-corrupt" | "lock-lost"; no breaking change to existing callers. 1.13.0 — MemoryOps.unimport (roll back the cards one import run created; archive-first soft delete without a registry tombstone, key freed for re-import); MemoryImportRequest.importRunId optional; MemoryOpErrorCode "lock-busy"; no breaking change to existing callers. 1.14.0 — additive complete vector-space identities, routes and degraded notes. 1.15.0 — HostServices.fetch? (HostFetch: every outbound engine HTTP request goes through it when set); SecretStore becomes resolve(ref, purpose) (lease() kept optional and deprecated; it was never called) for provider `apiKeyRef`; ProviderCredentialConfig, RemoteRerankerConfig and the reranker providers jina | voyage | remote with baseUrl/protocol; no breaking change to existing callers (the engine called no SecretStore member before 1.15.0). Also: MemoryImportRequest without importRunId attributes each card to the run its sourceRef names (`;run=<id>`); MemoryUnimportRequest.importRunId also selects such lines; MemoryUnimportResult.derived.graphEdgesRemoved? / mirrorsArchived? / cleanupErrors? (unimport drops the undone cards' graph edges and archives their Obsidian mirrors). 1.17.0 — AdminOps.reembedding.validate({ id }) (the coordinator's validating → ready_to_switch step: target generation check and semantic recall probe, so a host that owns its switch can finish a migration); a failed validation rejects and leaves the record in validating; no breaking change to existing callers. 1.16.0 — MemoryOps.link(id, req, p, a) (owner decision 2026-10-19: attach an imported duplicate to an existing card as an additional source instead of storing a duplicate; sidecar `_links/`, the card row is never written; idempotent per sourceRef); MemoryCard.links? (show/list); MemoryUnimportResult.links? (unimport of a run unlinks that run's links, the card stays); Engine.capabilities (EngineCapabilities, `memoryLink: true`); no breaking change to existing callers.

SecretStore.title: SecretStore

resolve.description: Resolve `ref` (the configured `apiKeyRef`, a name, never the value). Reject or return "" when unknown.

SecretStore.description: 1.15.0: the host's secret store. The engine calls `resolve` for every provider config that sets `apiKeyRef` — before `apiKeyEnv`/`apiKey`; with `apiKeyRef` set and no store (or a failed / empty resolution) the provider fails closed, it never falls back to the environment. The value is never logged, persisted or put into a cache key in clear (only hashed, as before); providers keep it at most 60 s (embedding, reranker) or not at all (LLM: per call) and drop it on HTTP 401/403, so a rotated key applies without a restart.

HostFetch.title: HostFetch
HostFetch.description: 1.15.0: WHATWG-fetch-compatible function. The engine passes `input` as a URL string and `init` with at least method, headers (plain object), body (string) and signal; it reads `ok`, `status`, `headers.get()`, `text()`/`json()` and `body` (ReadableStream, for size-capped reads) of the result.

RemoteRerankerConfig.description: 1.15.0: `config.reranker` for the HTTP providers. Presets (default baseUrl / protocol / model / env): cohere — https://api.cohere.com/v2, cohere, rerank-v3.5, COHERE_API_KEY; jina — https://api.jina.ai/v1, jina, jina-reranker-v2-base-multilingual, JINA_API_KEY; voyage — https://api.voyageai.com/v1, voyage, rerank-2.5, VOYAGE_API_KEY; remote — no defaults: baseUrl required, protocol "cohere", key optional (keyless self-hosted servers). The endpoint is `{baseUrl}/rerank` unless baseUrl already ends in /rerank. A failed rerank never switches to another model unless `fallbackProvider: "local-transformers"` is set; otherwise recall runs unreranked.

RecallQuery.title: RecallQuery

warmOnly.description: 1.9.0: run only the read-only heavy path (neo prelude reads, query embedding, read-only store open, vector search, rerank) and answer { blocks: [], degraded: null, timing } on success. Writes no memory data, no store, no file and no persistent embedding-cache row (embeds are memory-only, E5-R26), emits no event, never uses or fills the recall cache, never calls an LLM, runs at background (low, evictable) priority. It warms in-memory caches (the provider's embedding cache, loaded models, the neo worker); a cold local model cache still downloads model files, as any first model load does. A warm recall can also answer blocks [] with degraded "warm-failed" (the warm path failed), "aborted", "timeout", "queue-full" or "pressure" (shed at background priority), or "engine-closed"; a workspace whose policy disables memory answers an empty success.

EmbeddingService.description: probe(): exercises the provider once (a query embed of a fixed probe text with a per-engine nonce, so a persisted embedding cache cannot answer it) and memoizes a successful result; concurrent calls share one provider call; `refresh: true` forces a new provider call (queued behind a call already in flight, never answered by it). Never rejects for a provider failure (the result says `ok: false`) and has no timeout of its own: callers should pass a `signal` (the harness warm-up does); rejects with MemoryOpError `storage` ("engine is closed") after close(). serve(address): starts the engine's scoped-embedding IPC server on `address` (omitted → the platform default, `host.platform.ipcAddress(<baseDbPath>/control/embedding-ipc)`), without the loopback claim listener (ADR-001 C1). Idempotent for the address already served (same result object); `null` stops serving and resolves `{ address: null, tokenPath: null, identity: null }` (in-process only). `dispose()` stops that server if it is still the served one (fire and forget). close() stops serving. Rejects with MemoryOpError: `invalid-input` (malformed address, a kind the platform does not use, an unsafe socket directory), `conflict` (another address already served, the address in use, the host lifecycle owns the IPC, the engine is an IPC client), `storage` (closed, or the listener failed to start).

stats.description: 1.17.0: per-agent counters for visible cards only, at most 500 ids. Undefined ids reads persisted counters; unseen requested visible ids return zero.

promote.description: 1.17.0: foreground system/user host only. Uses schicht15 cap per invocation (0 unlimited), never invokes providers; only agent-private source rows.

share.description: `allowSensitive` is the caller's explicit confirmation after an `approval-required` refusal.

propose.description: File a change proposal against a shared copy the caller can read but does not own (`a.origin === "user"`).

proposals.accept.description: Sharer only (anyone else: `not-found`). Refreshes the copy with the proposal's text.

import.description: 1.11.0: ingest finished cards (text + provenance + source timestamp) without the live-store LLM merge. `p` is the operator; `req.principal` is the card ACL binding. Requires `a.origin === "system"` and `a.background === false`. At most 500 cards per call.

rebind.description: 1.12.0: attach user-scope cards of one channel identity to a harness user. `dryRun` defaults to true. Requires `a.origin === "system"` and `a.background === false`. Counters only; no card text or raw identity keys.

unbind.description: 1.12.0: restore the owner bindings recorded under `req.rebindId`. Cards written after that rebind are left alone. `dryRun` defaults to false.

unimport.description: 1.13.0: roll back the cards `import` created under `req.importRunId` for `req.agentId`. `dryRun` defaults to true. Requires `a.origin === "system"` and `a.background === false`. Ids, keys, counters and reason codes only.

link.description: 1.16.0: attach an additional source to the existing card `id` (an imported card that duplicates it) without changing its text, vector or row. Requires `a.origin === "system"` and `a.background === false` (`denied`). The card must be one the caller can `show`; otherwise `not-found` (also for an unknown id). Idempotent per sourceRef. Apply takes the per-agent import lock (`lock-busy` / `lock-lost`); more than 100 links on one card is `conflict`. Audit line `memory.linked`.

MemoryRecallStat.title: MemoryRecallStat

lastRecalledAt.description: Epoch milliseconds, null when this card has not been recalled.

MemoryRecallStat.description: Every member rejects with MemoryOpError `storage` ("engine is closed") after `Engine.close()`. `list` and `show` read the agent-private pool plus the workspace and user pools the principal can reach. `forget`, `correct` and `share` act on the caller's own agent-private cards. On a shared (workspace/user) copy (D31): `forget` by the sharing agent retracts the copy (archive-first, soft delete; `tombstoneId` is null because the original stays live); `correct` by the sharing agent refreshes it (corrects the original, shares the new version, then retracts the old copy; the result id is the new copy); any other agent answers `denied` and files `propose` instead; `share` of a copy is always `denied`. Proposals never change a memory until the sharer calls `proposals.accept`. A proposal belongs to the shared pool of its copy: `proposals.*` reach it only through a principal that can reach that pool (otherwise `list` omits it and `accept`/`reject` answer `not-found`).
